_comment: Measured digest-exemption register for verified sourceReferences whose body cannot
carry a contentDigest without false-positiving on every probe.
Why this file exists: docs/citation-verification-sop.md requires a dynamic body to
OMIT a contentDigest rather than record a value that will false-positive, while the
same SOP's undigested-verified ratchet fails the decay audit for any verified:true
reference without one. For a corpus that is 98.5% PubMed record pages those two rules
are mutually unsatisfiable: SOP-compliant verification guarantees a ratchet breach.
This register separates the two populations so the ratchet pins only debt a qualified
human can actually retire, while the exempt population stays reported and never silent.
Discipline:
- An entry records a MEASUREMENT about a source's transport behaviour, not a
verification decision. Pending measurements do not activate an exemption.
Qualified-human approval with reviewer and date is required before debt is waived.
It never sets verified, never authorises promotion, and
never substitutes for the qualified-human step in the SOP.
- Every entry must carry reproducible evidence (sample fetches, statuses, byte
lengths, distinct SHA-256 count) and an assessedOn date.
- Entries expire: scripts/audit-citation-decay.js flags an assessment older than
EXEMPTION_REASSESS_AFTER_DAYS so a host whose behaviour changed is re-measured.
- urlPattern must be as narrow as the evidence supports. The loader rejects a
pattern that matches a URL whose host differs from `host`, and the audit reports
how many references each entry covers so an over-broad entry is visible rather
than trusted.
- Where a deterministic alternative anchor exists it is recorded in
digestibleAlternative so the exempt source can still gain real drift coverage at
the next qualified-human verification instead of staying blind forever.

exemptions.summary: PubMed record pages are served to automated clients as an HTTP 203 JavaScript challenge interstitial whose challengeId is regenerated per request, so the body is never byte-stable and carries no article content to hash.
exemptions.sopBasis: docs/citation-verification-sop.md, 'Content digests and tiered staleness': dynamic pages whose body changes per fetch must not receive a digest; omit it rather than record a value that will false-positive.

assessment.method: Three sequential GETs per sample URL, 2s apart, redirect-followed, response bodies hashed with SHA-256 and compared. Repeated under the audit probe User-Agent, a desktop browser User-Agent and no User-Agent header; all three client shapes received the identical 5590-byte 203 interstitial.
assessment.notes: The interstitial's <title> is the bare hostname 'pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov', not the article title, and no abstract markup is present. HTTP 203 is by definition non-authoritative (RFC 9110: the payload was modified from the origin server's 200 response by a transforming proxy), so this body is not the source a verifier read. Corroborated independently by docs/liver-cancer-sarcopenia-citation-verification-2026-disposition.md, which records that PubMed HTML was bot-walled on 2026-10-03 and that metadata and abstracts were read through NCBI E-utilities instead.

digestibleAlternative.notes: NCBI E-utilities efetch returns the authoritative PubMed record for the same PMID as byte-stable XML containing ArticleTitle, Abstract, PMID, DOI and publication status, so a retraction or correction changes it. This is the anchor a qualified human should digest at the next verification of a PubMed source. It is recorded here as an available path only: no digest has been backfilled onto any existing reference, because a digest computed after the fact is not anchored to its recorded sourceCheckedOn date and the SOP forbids it.

review.note: The volatility measurement is reproducible and objective. The qualified-human sign-off recorded here is for accepting the exemption as standing digest policy for this source class, and for deciding whether future PubMed verifications digest the E-utilities anchor instead.

exemptions.summary: Requests for this eCFR current-section URL are redirected to a Federal Register unblock interstitial; the final HTTP 200 body is not the regulation, contains no 38 CFR 3.310 text, and varies across fetches, so no source digest can be captured from the reference URL.
exemptions.sopBasis: docs/citation-verification-sop.md, 'Content digests and tiered staleness': a source body that cannot be retrieved at the reference URL cannot receive a comparable contentDigest; the redirect target is not the source.

assessment.method: Three sequential GETs, 2s apart, redirect-followed, using the citation-decay-audit User-Agent with a 15s timeout and at most 5 redirects. Recorded the initial and final URLs, source and final HTTP statuses, final body bytes, SHA-256 hashes, and whether 38 CFR 3.310 text was present.
assessment.observedVaryingToken: Federal Register unblock interstitial body; no 38 CFR 3.310 regulation text is present.
assessment.notes: The 2026-10-10 assessment described an 85,108-byte eCFR HTML body whose only variation was a per-response CSP nonce. That was not reproduced on 2026-11-09. The reference URL now returns a 302 to https://unblock.federalregister.gov/, whose 10,596-byte HTTP 200 body also contains a CSP nonce but no 3.310 text. This proposal therefore records a redirect/interstitial block, not eCFR body volatility, and must not be approved as the earlier nonce-only proposal. Covers one verified reference (38 CFR 3.310, ocd.json).

review.note: HOLD: this is a redirect-to-unblock observation, not the original nonce-only eCFR-body claim. A qualified human must decide whether to approve this narrower interstitial exemption or require a stable official eCFR rendering. No digest or source verification is recorded.

exemptions.summary: Oxford Academic serves automated clients an HTTP 403 bot-wall interstitial with a per-request varying body, so neither the article content nor a stable digest is obtainable by probe.
exemptions.sopBasis: docs/citation-verification-sop.md, 'Content digests and tiered staleness': dynamic pages whose body changes per fetch must not receive a digest; omit it rather than record a value that will false-positive.

assessment.method: Three sequential GETs, 2s apart, redirect-followed, bodies hashed with SHA-256 and compared.
assessment.observedVaryingToken: 403 bot-wall interstitial body carrying a per-request varying token
assessment.notes: HTTP 403 is already classified bot-blocked by the decay probe's BODY_FETCH_FALLBACK_STATUSES path, so this entry does not change link-rot accounting; it records that no digest can be captured for this source class by automated means. Covers one verified reference (hyperaldosteronism.json).

review.note: A qualified human reading this article in a browser may be able to capture a digest of the rendered article HTML; that decision is theirs and is not recorded here.
